changes.after: Read a property under a new name, supply a default, and collect the other properties.

before: In const {name: title} = object, name is the source property and title is the new local variable. This does not rename object.name. The earlier destructuring lesson introduced extraction; this one adds aliases, defaults and a remaining-properties object.

The pattern {name: title = "Untitled"} uses the default when name is absent or undefined, not when it is null or an empty string. The rest pattern ...rest collects remaining own enumerable properties into a new object.

summarizeNote reads name into title and puts other properties in rest. The outer rest object is new, but nested object values remain shared references. Destructuring is not a deep clone and does not remove properties from the source. JSON.stringify(value) formats these simple arrays/objects as JSON text for display; it returns a string and does not edit the value.
Implement summarizeNote(note) using the alias/default/rest pattern. Return {title, rest}. Keep null and empty names unchanged and leave the source object intact.
after:
In `{ name: title }`, `name` is the property to read and `title` is the local name to create. That new name is an alias.

The original object's `name` property is not renamed.

`{ name: title = "Untitled" }` uses the default only when `name` is missing or undefined. Null and empty text stay as they are.

`...rest` collects the other properties in a new object. It skips inherited properties and those marked to stay out of normal listing.

The outer `rest` object is new, but any objects inside it are still shared. This is a shallow copy, not a deep clone.

The source keeps its properties. `JSON.stringify` shows these simple results as JSON text.

Complete `summarizeNote(note)` with the alias, default, and rest pattern. Return `{ title, rest }`.

Keep the source unchanged, including when the name is null or empty.

before.question: If note.name is null, what value does title receive?
before.explanation: A destructuring default replaces undefined, not null. The alias changes the local binding name, not the value.

after.question: If note.name is null, what value does title receive?
after.explanation: Null is a supplied value. The default applies only when the property is missing or undefined.
